title: Pune dev-tool hit 18K signups on community + content, then stalled at 1.9% free-to-paid
content: A Pune API-observability SaaS (Postman-adjacent, for backend teams) had a 4-person team and ₹90K/month — too small to fight global incumbents on Meta/Google CPMs. Situation: paid CAC for 'developer' intent on Google ran ₹4,200-6,000 per signup, completely unaffordable on that budget. Action: they went fully bottom-up. Open-sourced the CLI on GitHub (3,100 stars in 7 months), shipped 2 deep technical posts/week on Dev.to and Hashnode (real debugging guides, never product pitches), ran a 1,400-member Discord, and launched a no-card free tier. Founders answered every GitHub issue within 6 hours. Result: 18,200 signups in 9 months at a blended ₹38/signup with near-zero paid; organic search drove 61% of traffic. Then the stall: free-to-paid conversion sat at just 1.9% (a healthy SaaS band is 3-5%) because the free tier solved the entire job for solo devs — there was no seats, SSO, or retention paywall to force a team upgrade. They had built a huge unmonetised audience. Lesson: community-led PLG buys cheap top-of-funnel, but without a designed 'team moment' the funnel never monetises.
lesson: Cheap community-led signups mean nothing without a designed 'team moment' — a collaboration, seat, or compliance trigger that forces the free-to-paid upgrade. Architect the paywall around team usage before you scale the funnel, not after.
